The SOURCE carries four NON-BREAKING spaces (` `), because four ordinary spaces collapse to one in HTML and the blessed layout draws a gap; that byte-form is pinned in `design_polish.rs`. WebDriver's rendered-text extraction NORMALISES U+00A0 to U+0020, so what the USER'S SCREEN yields here is four ORDINARY spaces. Both pins are correct and neither is redundant: the source pin catches the gap being written the collapsing way, and this pin catches it not reaching the screen. ⚠ My first expectation here asserted the non-breaking form and this step caught it — measured, then corrected against the instrument rather than guessed a second time.

══ NA-0766 (`D-0043`) — I3: A NAME IS REQUIRED ══ Item 10. Activate stays disabled until the field holds a real name after trimming, and the DISABLED CONTROL IS THE WHOLE ENFORCEMENT — there is no error text by design. ⚠ WHY THE ENVIRONMENT IS SET FROM SCRIPT AND NOT THROUGH THE UI: persisting a relay requires a SUCCESSFUL PROBE (NA-0754's test-and-save-on-proof invariant) and the desktop harness has no fixture relay (`ENG-0226`, open), so the relay cause would mask the name cause forever. Only the environment fact is synthesized; the gate itself is the PRODUCT'S OWN `inviteSyncActivate()`, driven for real — the same idiom `f_n` uses to reach the contacts render.

NA-0778 (004d / RULING_NA0778_009 R61) -- THE CREATE FIELD ENFORCES THE REDEEM SIDE's GRAMMAR. A name with a space minted an invitation every accept of which failed at the inviter's provisioning (the engine's channel_label_ok), silently, forever. Now: 'Flight B' -> Activate disabled and the muted hint visible, the typed value UNTOUCHED; 'Flight-B' -> enabled, the hint hidden; the field carries the app's 32-character cap.

⚠ NO ERROR TEXT FOR THE EMPTY-NAME CAUSE -- item 10 says the disabled control is the WHOLE enforcement there. NA-0778 (004d / RULING_NA0778_009 R61) adds the ILLEGAL-name cause, which DOES carry a muted hint: see the rows above. ⚠ AND NO ERROR TEXT APPEARS FOR THE NAME CAUSE — item 10 says the disabled control is the WHOLE enforcement. ⚠ MY FIRST FORM OF THIS STEP ASSERTED THAT NO HINT WAS VISIBLE AND THE INSTRUMENT CAUGHT IT: the no-relay hint IS legitimately on screen here, because the harness genuinely has no relay (`ENG-0226`), and that is a DIFFERENT cause with a message of its own. The property actually ordered is that the NAME cause adds nothing — so it is measured as what it is: the VISIBLE SET must be identical with an empty name and with a valid one. Corrected against the measurement rather than guessed a second time.

steps.text: ══ NA-0766 (`D-0043`) — I6: POST-ACTIVATION LOCKS ══ Item 12. One invite per window: Activate is disabled, the name field is read-only showing what the invite was minted with, and a second press cannot mint. Before this lane `inviteRefresh()` RE-ENABLED the control after a successful mint, so a second press burned a second slot — this is a slot-accounting fix, not a cosmetic one.
⚠ THE LATCH SURVIVES A REFRESH, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT — the old defect was that the refresh undid the disable. Driven: re-run the ONE decision and confirm the control stays down.
⚠ AND THE SLOT IS NOT BURNED TWICE: a click on the disabled control changes nothing. The code in the box is the one already minted.

══ NA-0766 (`D-0043`) — I4's CAN-FAIL ARM AT THE TENTH-INVITE BOUNDARY ══ Ordered by ruling Q4. This is the ONE place the old shape moved: `inviteRefresh()` recomputed the cap after every mint, so minting the TENTH invite made the cap line APPEAR after activation. The cap is now decided ONCE at open and held for the window's life. Driven AT the boundary, because an instrument that never reaches the boundary cannot fail there.

══ NA-0766 (`D-0043`) — I5: THE COPY CYCLE ══ Item 13, which measured ALREADY SHIPPED EXACTLY AS ORDERED and is therefore NOT rebuilt. This lane's obligation is to carry it UNBROKEN through item 6's restructure, so it is pinned here for the first time rather than assumed: click → 'copied' → reverts on its own → clickable again, indefinitely. ⚠ NO SLEEP (brief sec 8): the revert is awaited with the harness's bounded `poll_exec`, which is the shipped polling idiom, not a timer. ⚠ The clipboard API's reachability in this harness was MEASURED before this block was written, not assumed.
⚠ AND IT REVERTS ON ITS OWN — the acknowledgement is temporary by design, so the control returns to being an offer rather than a report.
⚠ AND IT IS REUSABLE INDEFINITELY — nothing disables it, so a second click behaves exactly like the first. That is what makes it the recovery path when the single-gesture copy could not copy.
